biomass-energy-carbon.alt: A cycle of four boxes. Growing plants store carbon in wood and crops by photosynthesis; an arrow labeled years to decades leads to harvest of wood, crop waste, manure, corn or sugarcane; then to burning or converting into heat, electricity or liquid fuels such as ethanol and biodiesel; an arrow labeled released in hours leads to carbon dioxide in the air with smoke and soot; an arrow back to growing plants says taken back up only if plants regrow. A banner says cleared and not regrown, the carbon stays in the air and habitat is lost.
